title: feat(ui,app): wire browser app tracing, dropped model bytes, and inline CpuEye fallback
body:
## What changed

- Added `camcraft_app::logging::dispatch(writer, browser)` using `.without_time().with_ansi(false)` for browser builds, and called `camcraft_app::logging::init()` inside `camcraft_start` (`crates/app/src/logging.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_web.rs`).
- Updated `file_drop::take_drop` with `check_drop_bytes` and `deliver_model_bytes` to load bare-name dropped model bytes through `file_pick::deliver` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/file_drop.rs`).
- Refactored `CpuEye` into `Mode::Threaded` and `Mode::Inline(Box<Inline>)` sharing `march_job`, falling back to `CpuEye::inline()` on `wasm32` or `ErrorKind::Unsupported` (`crates/ui/src/trace/cpu_eye.rs`).
- Added `StockEye::cpu_pending` and requested frame repaints in `WebShell::ui` while inline marching is pending (`crates/ui/src/trace/eye.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_web.rs`).
- Recorded the design choices in `docs/decisions/31-wasm-browser-runtime.md`.

## Cause

- `camcraft_start` did not initialize `camcraft_app::logging`, and default `tracing_subscriber::fmt` emits ANSI escapes and calls `SystemTime::now()`, which panics on `wasm32`.
- `file_drop::take_drop` routed bare-name browser drops into `classify`, which refused them because `path.is_file()` is false in browser builds.
- `CpuEye::spawn` failed without OS threads, and `WebShell::ui` did not poll pending CPU work for repaints.

## Tests

- Pins (red before fix, green after fix):
  - `crates/app/tests/logging.rs::browser_subscriber_omits_timestamps_and_ansi_escapes` (red before fix: E0425 compile error; green after fix)
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/file_drop.rs`: `a_bare_name_dropped_mesh_with_bytes_imports_and_undoes`, `a_bare_name_drop_with_bad_extension_or_read_error_is_refused_by_name` (red before fix: `drop refused: cube.stl is not a readable file`; green after fix)
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/browser_files.rs::browser_shell_initializes_app_logging_and_repaints_pending_cpu_eye` (red before fix: assertion failed; green after fix)
  - `crates/ui/src/trace/cpu_eye.rs::tests::inline_cpu_eye_marches_without_spawning_a_thread` (red before fix: E0599 compile error; green after fix)
- Mutations (file reverted to `upstream/main` -> red, restored -> green):
  - `crates/app/src/logging.rs`: red (compile error) / green
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_web.rs`: red / green
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/file_drop.rs`: red / green
  - `crates/ui/src/trace/cpu_eye.rs`: red (compile error) / green
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, after final edit):
  - `camcraft-app` lib: `352 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored` (`a_smooth_face_needing_more_than_the_old_cap_is_divided_not_tripped`, heavy lane)
  - `camcraft-app` `logging`: `5 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored`
  - `camcraft-ui` lib: `952 passed; 0 failed; 6 ignored` (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `review_1710_wcs_page_and_viewport_evidence`, `tool_editor_snapshot`, `a_full_length_jump_on_the_worker_costs_no_more_than_the_direct_seek`, `traced_playback_cost_per_frame_and_per_jump`)
  - `camcraft-ui` integration suites: `boundary` (`3 passed`), `boundary_picks` (`6 passed`), `sinker_setup` (`2 passed`), `tap_hand` (`3 passed`), `theme_files` (`15 passed`), `trace_composite` (`4 passed`), `trace_parity` (`5 passed`), `waterjet_tool` (`1 passed`); `0 failed; 0 ignored`
- Clippy (`cargo xtask gate batch --only clippy`, `-D warnings` across all 8 workspace crates `--all-targets`): passed in 3s (`0 failed`).

## Browser evidence (review follow-up)

The before/after pairs show browser dropped-file import and CPU stock preview. The PR source and head remain unchanged at `28d3295ba3f2e4e3e24c5600abb5b77059d5f1af`. These are actual browser captures, not native snapshots.

Build: debug `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with `web/build-app-wasm.sh`, Rust 1.99.1, Clang 21, WASI SDK 34 sysroot and wasm-bindgen 0.2.129. Both browsers ran on Linux at 1440 × 1000, device scale 1.

The before build is a temporary source copy of this head with `crates/ui/src/egui_app/file_drop.rs`, `crates/ui/src/trace/cpu_eye.rs` and `crates/ui/src/trace/eye.rs` taken from its parent `a529c455352d8c2d228e3dd83d0e5d42a91ea9b0`, and the pending-CPU repaint clause removed from `shell_web.rs`. It retains this PR's browser logging initialization and formatter so startup succeeds and the import and CPU regressions can be isolated. The after build uses the unchanged PR head.

Browser import: Chromium 159.0.8154.6, headless ANGLE SwiftShader, with WebGPU disabled so the app uses WebGL2. Both captures drop the same in-memory `browser-block.stl` file (a 30 × 20 × 10 mm cuboid) onto the canvas.

| Before: bare-name browser drop refused | After: model imported from browser bytes |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: browser drop refused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eb739294174052ce25c2a274dc3f5bbf59c4b984/2239/import-before.png) | ![After: browser model imported](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eb739294174052ce25c2a274dc3f5bbf59c4b984/2239/import-after.png) |

CPU stock preview: Firefox 159.0, headless WebGPU with Mesa Vulkan llvmpipe (Mesa 26.0.8). WebGPU preferences were `dom.webgpu.enabled=true`, `gfx.webgpu.force-enabled=true` and `dom.webgpu.allow-software-adapter=true`; the process used `MOZ_DISABLE_CONTENT_SANDBOX=1` and `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/lvp_icd.json`. Both captures open the same generated project (closed cuboid model, 40 × 40 × 10 mm box stock, Ø6 end mill and one 2D Contour), regenerate the stale operation, then click Deviate.

To exercise the CPU fallback on this working WebGPU adapter, both stock runs use the same browser-side hook: `GPUDevice.prototype.createShaderModule` replaces only shader descriptors whose label is `trace` with the invalid WGSL string `controlled_trace_validation_refusal`. The app's existing validation error scope reports that the compute kernel was refused and that the CPU march stands in. The composite pipeline is untouched. This hook changes no production source and is disclosed because these captures demonstrate controlled fallback, not a naturally failing adapter.

| Before: CPU worker cannot start in the browser | After: inline CPU preview renders |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: CPU stock preview refused](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eb739294174052ce25c2a274dc3f5bbf59c4b984/2239/stock-before.png) | ![After: inline CPU stock preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/eb739294174052ce25c2a274dc3f5bbf59c4b984/2239/stock-after.png) |

The before stock capture retains the transparent stock sheet; its browser console reports `cpu eye: the worker would not start: operation not supported on this platform`. The after stock capture shows the coarse CPU preview and the Deviate result: REST 729 cells, 512.58 mm³, worst 5.00 mm. The images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch. No screenshots, logs or review evidence were committed to the PR branch. This follow-up changes only the PR body and adds no code or tests requiring a new mutation check. Existing pins are `a_bare_name_dropped_mesh_with_bytes_imports_and_undoes`, `inline_cpu_eye_marches_without_spawning_a_thread` and `browser_shell_initializes_app_logging_and_repaints_pending_cpu_eye`; the original code mutation results remain listed above.

## Goldens moved

- `none` (`git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- Live browser import and a controlled CPU stock-preview fallback were exercised as documented above. A natural device rejection of the trace kernel was not available on the working WebGPU adapter, so that fallback evidence uses the disclosed browser-side validation fault injection.
- Remaining `#31` work deferred to separate PRs: inline `PlayWorker` fallback in `stock_play_worker.rs` (overlapped by `#2192`), `shell.rs` viewport split (overlapped by `#2110` and `#1330`), and removing `#![cfg_attr(target_arch = "wasm32", allow(dead_code))]` in `crates/ui/src/lib.rs`.

## Overlaps

- PR `#2150` touches `crates/ui/src/egui_app/file_drop.rs` in `MESH_EXTENSIONS`, `classify`, and its tests; this PR touches `take_drop` and adds `check_drop_bytes` and `deliver_model_bytes` (different functions; whichever merges second refreshes).

Changelog: Browser builds now route app tracing to the console without panicking, load dropped model files from bytes, and fall back to inline CPU stock preview when threads cannot spawn.

Effort: high

Refs #31
